proposal: The Mandate recommends that HRSA use notice-and-comment rulemaking to update the women's preventive services mandate; rescind its contracts with the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists and set up a Federal Advisory Committee Act compliant advisory committee; include fertility awareness-based methods and supplies; remove male condoms; and remove ulipristal (Ella) from the contraceptive mandate (pp. 484 to 485).
remaining: Notice-and-comment rulemaking to repromulgate the women's preventive services mandate (none found; the 2025 to 2026 cervical screening update used a Federal Register comment notice, not a rule; p. 484)
Rescission of the ACOG-linked cooperative agreements and a FACA-compliant advisory committee (none found; guidelines still developed through the Women's Preventive Services Initiative; p. 484)
Express coverage of fertility awareness-based method supplies (the guideline includes instruction in these methods but supplies were not found; p. 485)
Removal of condoms from the guidelines (still listed; p. 485)
Removal of ulipristal from the contraceptive mandate (still listed; p. 485)

flags: Introduced bills found (Right to Contraception Act, H.R. 8083) run toward wider contraceptive access; none is enacted or operative, so they do not support diverged.
review.mandate_note: Pages 484 to 485 recommend notice-and-comment repromulgation, ending the ACOG-linked arrangement in favor of a FACA-compliant committee, covering fertility awareness methods and supplies, and removing male condoms and ulipristal; the proposal matches.

status_summary: No rulemaking, advisory committee change or revision of the contraception guideline was found. HRSA's guidelines page (last reviewed December 2025) lists one update in the period, a cervical cancer screening change put out for comment in the Federal Register on 2025-10-01 and finalized in a notice published 2026-01-05, developed through the Women's Preventive Services Initiative under HRSA cooperative agreements. The contraception guideline still references the December 2021 FDA Birth Control Guide, which lists condoms and ulipristal acetate. The Supreme Court decided Kennedy v. Braidwood Management on 2025-06-27, upholding the Secretary's appointment of Task Force members, without addressing HRSA recommendations.
title: Repromulgate the women's preventive services mandate; revise the contraceptive guidelines
uncertainties: Checked systematically on 2026-10-18. The Federal Register API check (women's preventive services filtered to HRSA, contraceptive coverage rules and proposed rules, and a variant on contraceptive guidelines and HRSA) found only the October 2025 comment request and January 2026 notice on cervical cancer screening and CMS information collections that describe the existing religious and moral exemptions; nothing revises the contraception guideline or repromulgates the mandate by rule. The Unified Agenda check was partial: only the Federal Register fallback was usable, with no rule or proposed rule found. The Congress check, run in review as one search limited to congress.gov and govinfo.gov, found bills that would protect or widen contraceptive access (the Right to Contraception Act in both chambers, and H.R. 8083 on access to oral contraceptives with a GAO study, whose status record was read); none revises the HRSA guidelines along the lines recommended and none is enacted. The agency check re-read the HRSA guidelines page (last reviewed December 2025): condoms and ulipristal acetate remain listed, fertility awareness instruction is listed without supplies, and the guidelines are still developed through the Women's Preventive Services Initiative under HRSA cooperative agreements; whether those agreements still run through ACOG was not checked. The news check found no 2025 or 2026 report of a revised contraception guideline. The Supreme Court opinion concerns the Preventive Services Task Force; KFF reports HRSA and ACIP claims returned to the district court, not independently checked. The 2025-08-13 vacatur of the exemption rules is tracked in c14-57.
